security_frame.attacker: Software running on the Caliptra core at any stage of the boot flow, including a compromised or simply buggy mutable firmware image that misreports which boot phase it is in.
security_frame.precondition: A released reset with the core fetching from ICCM. No special mode is needed; the condition is the ordinary boot sequence.
security_frame.input: Whatever the running firmware chooses to write to the phase-indicating register fields. There is no hardware observation of fetch behaviour to contradict it.
security_frame.protected_asset: The trustworthiness of the boot-phase signal that downstream policy depends on. Key vault access rules, OCP lock behaviour and the crypto blocks' phase-dependent policy are only as trustworthy as the event that tells them which phase the system is in.
security_frame.security_property: The boot phase must be derived by hardware from observable behaviour, such as instruction fetch entering a configured FMC or RT ICCM region, so that software cannot claim to be in a phase it has not reached.
security_frame.implemented_logic: No hardware-derived boot-phase event exists. The transition detector source file is absent from src/integration/rtl, and grep across the entire src tree returns zero references to boot_flow at any level, so no dangling instance or unconnected port survives. The only phase-adjacent signal reaching the crypto blocks is ss_ocp_lock_in_progress, assigned in src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_top.sv directly from the SS_OCP_LOCK_CTRL.LOCK_IN_PROGRESS software register field, and the ICCM lock is likewise assigned from the internal_iccm_lock software field.

security_feature_bypassed: Hardware derivation of the boot phase. With no transition detector, every phase-dependent policy in the design rests on software self-reporting.
proof_goal: Establish on one unmodified checkout that no hardware-derived boot-phase event exists, that the removal is complete rather than a half-disconnected remnant, and that every surviving phase-adjacent signal originates in a software-written register field.
proof_style: Scripted structural census of one real checkout, paired with a negative control that reconstructs the shape of the missing detector on a scratch copy of the tree and requires the identical census to fail.
invariant: A security decision that depends on the boot phase must not take the phase from the entity whose behaviour it is meant to constrain.
minimum_attack_sequence: Firmware running before it has legitimately entered a later boot phase writes the phase-indicating register field to claim that phase.
No hardware observes instruction fetch to contradict the claim, because the detector that would have done so does not exist.
Every consumer of that signal, including the four crypto blocks that receive it, applies the policy for the claimed phase.
controls: The integration top is present and contains live debug gating, so the census reads real code rather than a stale or empty tree.
The CPU wrapper is instantiated, so the fetch-side logic the detector would have observed does exist.
The key vault is instantiated in the integration top, so its port list is the live one.
The key vault does take a firmware-update reset window input and a debug-unlock or scan mode input, so it is capable of receiving control inputs; the boot-phase input specifically is missing.
The key vault description names the software bit as the phase indicator and states the obligation as a software requirement, which confirms the design intends a phase signal to exist.
witness_construction_note: No dynamic witness is possible and none is claimed. Absence here is total: the module, its instance and every textual reference are gone, so the elaborated design contains nothing that can be driven to expose the omission. There is no tied-off output to observe stuck low and no dangling port to stimulate. Because a simulation cannot carry the claim, the negative control does the work a witness normally would: it reconstructs the shape of the missing logic on a scratch copy and shows the census detects its return, which is what makes the passing census on the submitted checkout non-vacuous.
expected_evidence: The transition detector source file does not exist.
Zero files under src reference boot_flow, and none of the three phase outputs is referenced anywhere.
The integration top does not instantiate the detector and no dangling port declaration survives.
The key vault module references no boot-flow signal, while it does take other control inputs.
The OCP lock phase signal is assigned directly from a software register field and is not derived from any fetch or ICCM observation.
That software-written signal is distributed to at least five consumers in the integration top.
The ICCM lock is likewise assigned from a software register field.
With the detector reconstructed on a scratch tree, the census fails on the absence gates while the anchors and software-origin gates stay green.
success_criteria: All structural gates pass on the unmodified checkout.
The negative control fails the census after reconstructing the detector.
The negative control's failures are confined to the census gates, leaving the anchors and the software-origin gates green.
The negative control verifies the submitted checkout is unmodified afterwards.
non_findings: No claim that the OCP lock register is itself incorrectly implemented. Its sticky write-once behaviour is correct for a software-set field.
No claim about the downstream policy in the key vault or the crypto blocks. Those are separate cases; this one is about the absence of the event they would consume.
No claim that a specific exploit was executed. No simulation was run and none is possible for this omission.
No claim that the ICCM lock is defective; it is noted only as a second phase-adjacent control with the same software origin.
